investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T23:18–23:26Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable, preventing VM assignment and blocking the eval from collecting any required evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is never scheduled.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (e.g., a kata/peerpods node pool label). If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, scheduling is impossible regardless of overall cluster size (failed-check.message).

Tertiary — cluster autoscaler not configured or not yet triggered: no new kata.peerpods-capable node was provisioned within the 137–146s window before the eval timed out, suggesting autoscaling is absent, slow, or at a quota ceiling.
Lower confidence — a recent workload surge or leaked/stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new allocations.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T23:21–23:26Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval pod could not be scheduled, the remote agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state check received zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and cannot be used as fallback. Preemption was also ruled out by the scheduler (no preemption victims found). As a result, every eval attempt to create a remote agent pod timed out unscheduled (~137–151 s), preventing the probe from reaching the state-polling stage and producing any evidence. The contract gap (missing orgId, agentId, readyState, state — evidenced by expected-output.missing-required-evidence) is a downstream symptom of the scheduling failure, not an independent code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads (eval or production) have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the probe pod.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's required node selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, amplifying the impact of any VM slot exhaustion.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 6-node cluster may be insufficient to absorb both steady-state workloads and observability probe pods simultaneously.

Lower probability — a recent change to pod resource requests or node affinity labels (not evidenced in suspectChanges, which is empty) could have tightened scheduling constraints, but no such change is present in the supplied source discovery artifacts.

The pod remained Unschedulable for 146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; it is not a code defect in the eval runner or the expected-output contract. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T23:18–23:26Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable, preventing VM assignment and blocking the eval from collecting any required evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (e.g., a kata/peerpods node pool label). If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, scheduling is impossible regardless of overall cluster size (failed-check.message).

Tertiary — cluster autoscaler not configured or not yet triggered: no new kata.peerpods-capable node was provisioned within the 137–146s window before the eval timed out, suggesting autoscaling is absent, slow, or at a quota ceiling.
Lower confidence — a recent workload surge or leaked/stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new allocations.

followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API (or a cluster metrics endpoint) for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested counts across all nodes, so VM slot exhaustion is detected before probe pods are submitted.

Add a pre-flight scheduling check eval that submits a dry-run pod (--dry-run=server) with the remote agent's resource requests and node affinity, and fails fast with a clear capacity message rather than waiting for a scheduling timeout.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts at least N nodes match the remote agent pod's required node selector, alerting when the schedulable pool drops below a safe threshold.

Introduce a historical baseline for the remote-agents feature checks so that currentlyRegressedFromPass can be populated in future runs, enabling regression detection rather than only point-in-time failure detection.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never received a running agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was produced and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available cluster nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. The pod remained Unschedulable for 146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; it is not a code defect in the eval runner or the expected-output contract. No evidence of a user-facing incident or real-traffic impact is present in the supplied packet.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId; a scheduling failure at this call would prevent all downstream evidence collection.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 capable nodes: the VM pool is fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the selector was recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective pool may have shrunk.

Tertiary — concurrent eval or workload contention: if multiple eval runs or production workloads simultaneously requested kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the pool could be transiently exhausted rather than permanently depleted.

Lower probability — VM pool autoscaler not triggering or lagging: if the cluster relies on a node autoscaler to provision additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, a delay or failure in autoscaling would produce this symptom.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 capable nodes immediately to determine whether the pool is fully consumed by active, stuck, or leaked pods.
Check for any remote agent pods left in a non-terminal state (Running, Pending, or Unknown) from prior eval runs or production workloads that may be holding VM slots without releasing them.
If VM slots are confirmed exhausted by leaked or zombie pods, terminate those pods to restore scheduling capacity and re-run the eval to verify recovery.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods to confirm that only 2 of 6 nodes are intended to be eligible; if the pool should be larger, investigate whether node labels have drifted or whether additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes need to be provisioned.
Assess whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool has a cluster autoscaler configured and, if so, whether it is functioning correctly and has headroom to add capacity.

Monitor the remote-agents feature status after remediation; note that remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true in infra/evals/status/features.json (lines 183-184), so sustained failures on those checks will contribute to feature degraded/outage classification per the degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not fully consumed on the 2 capable nodes, the scheduling failure would have a different root cause (e.g., a quota, admission webhook, or runtime class misconfiguration).

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence fields, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., concurrent workload contention) rather than a sustained capacity deficit.

If the node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod was recently changed to exclude nodes that previously matched, the root cause would shift to a configuration drift rather than VM pool exhaustion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and the selector is the sole blocker, the diagnosis would shift from capacity exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration as the primary cause.

If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) also failed at the same time with a different error, it would suggest a broader API or authentication failure rather than a VM-pool-specific issue.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on each capable node and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion.

Add an eval that counts remote agent pods in non-terminal states (Pending, Running) and alerts if the count approaches the total VM slot capacity, catching slot leaks before they block new scheduling.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is at or above a minimum threshold, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.

Consider a canary eval that attempts to schedule a minimal remote agent pod on a short timeout and reports the scheduler outcome (Scheduled vs. Unschedulable) as a leading indicator, separate from the full runtime flow eval.
